lines: I’ve gotten used to being alive.
I’m bored with walking.
I’ve started stopping more.
I quit trying to begin.
I didn’t understand.
I wanted something.
What was it that I wanted?
I didn’t understand.
“Do your best,” the admirable ones would tell me.
It’s sickening.
I’m done with cheap words, sweet words.
I don’t need them.
Crying, getting hurt.
I even grew to hate breathing.
Probably, that’s it.
Even now, forever.
I’ve been searching for words that could let me escape.
Ah, would that be fine?
“Is it okay now?” I wondered.
Is someone like me just hopeless?
Tomorrow presses in, pushing me aside.
I have no sin, do I?
From now on.
The false mask of “from now on” has stopped coming off.
Ah, whatever, it’s fine, whatever.
To the retreating back I say,
“Good‑bye.”
It’s a neatly dressed thing, isn’t it?
All lined up beautifully, it must have felt good.
Compared to this world,
I felt I could still breathe better underwater.
I’ve been thinking this for a long time.
I’m fed up.
Help me with your sweet words.
Cheap words are fine, you hypocrite.
Today I grind my teeth again.
What am I supposed to live for?
“Until the next time,” “until the next time,”
It’s been built by forcing myself.
Ah, that’s nice, isn’t it?
You’re fine, aren’t you?
I watched the back of you, who I could never catch up to.
Tomorrow presses in, pushing me aside.
I have no sin, do I?
The false mask of “from now on” has stopped coming off.
Ah, would that be fine?
“It’s fine now?” I wondered.
It’s still not too late, right? Don’t leave me behind.
Prologue

You, me, both lost.
